skill.name: dogfood
skill.description: Systematically explore and test a web application to find bugs, UX issues, and other problems. Use when asked to "dogfood", "QA", "exploratory test", "find issues", "bug hunt", "test this app/site/platform", or review the quality of a web application. Produces a structured report with full reproduction evidence -- step-by-step screenshots, repro videos, and detailed repro steps for every issue -- so findings can be handed directly to the responsible teams.
skill.summary: Guides black-box web app dogfooding and produces reports with screenshots, videos, and reproducible issue steps.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown examples or expected browser-testing command snippets, and many were false positives. Confirmed risks remain around agent-browser command execution, local evidence capture, filesystem writes, and authenticated session handling. Semantic review found no prompt injection text, but it did find over-broad npx permission plus credential and auth-state exposure concerns.

remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash(npx agent-browser:*) from allowed-tools and allow only the direct agent-browser binary needed by the workflow.

remediation.issue: Credentials are passed as shell arguments
remediation.suggestion: Use a secure credential input path that avoids command-line arguments, shell history, and process listings.

remediation.issue: Authenticated browser state is saved to user-selected paths
remediation.suggestion: Store auth-state files in a restricted directory, document that they may contain tokens, and provide cleanup guidance.

remediation.issue: Screenshots and videos may capture sensitive application data
remediation.suggestion: Add redaction guidance and warn users to avoid capturing secrets, personal data, and production-only information.

remediation.issue: User-controlled placeholders are used in shell examples
remediation.suggestion: Validate target URLs, session names, and output paths, and quote shell arguments consistently in all examples.

semantic_findings.title: Over-broad npx Command Permission
semantic_findings.description: The tool allowlist permits Bash(npx agent-browser:*), even though the instructions say to use agent-browser directly. npx can fetch or execute a package from the network if invoked.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 4 grants npx execution while line 25 only discourages it in prose. The enforceable allowlist remains broader than the documented safe path.

semantic_findings.title: Credentials Passed Through Shell Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The login workflow fills email and password values through command-line arguments. Those values can appear in shell history, process listings, or command logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The password placeholder is passed directly in an agent-browser fill command. Command-line secret exposure is a common and concrete risk.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Auth State in User-selected Output Directory
semantic_findings.description: The skill saves authenticated browser state to {OUTPUT_DIR}/auth-state.json and allows /tmp/qa as an output example. It also tells users not to delete output files, which can leave session tokens on disk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The state save command likely stores cookies or session tokens in a caller-selected directory. The guidance to preserve output files increases persistence of sensitive artifacts.

content.user_title: Test Web Apps with Repro Evidence
content.value_statement: Teams often miss UI, workflow, and console defects before release. This skill explores a web app and produces reproducible evidence for each issue.
actual_capabilities: Opens a target web app in an agent-browser session.
Creates a dogfood report from the included Markdown template.
Tests navigation, forms, states, responsiveness, and console errors.
Captures annotated screenshots for visible and step-based issues.
Records repro videos for interactive or stateful defects.
Summarizes issue severity counts and reproduction steps.
limitations: Requires agent-browser and access to the target URL.
Tests the app as a user and does not inspect source code.
Authenticated flows need user-provided credentials or OTP codes.
Screenshots, videos, and auth state may contain sensitive data.

use_cases.title: Pre-release QA pass
use_cases.description: Run a structured exploratory test on a staging app before a release candidate is approved.

use_cases.title: Product workflow review
use_cases.description: Validate core onboarding, billing, or dashboard flows and collect evidence for triage.

use_cases.title: Frontend regression hunt
use_cases.description: Check changed UI areas for broken controls, visual defects, console errors, and accessibility issues.

prompt_templates.title: Dogfood a public page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: quick black-box review of a public site.
prompt_templates.prompt: Dogfood https://example.com and create a report with screenshots for every issue you find.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on one product area
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: test a specific workflow or section.
prompt_templates.prompt: Dogfood https://staging.example.com. Focus on signup, onboarding, and account settings. Use the default output directory.

prompt_templates.title: Test an authenticated flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review a signed-in experience with user-provided credentials.
prompt_templates.prompt: Dogfood https://staging.example.com after signing in with the test account I provide. Ask me for any OTP code when needed.

prompt_templates.title: Run a scoped release audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: collect evidence for release triage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Dogfood https://preview.example.com with session release-candidate. Focus on checkout, billing settings, and mobile responsiveness. Produce repro videos for interactive issues.

output_examples.input: Dogfood a staging checkout flow before launch.
output_examples.output: A report with severity counts, issue titles, affected URLs, repro steps, annotated screenshots, and videos for interactive failures.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard for UX and console problems.
output_examples.output: A triage-ready summary of navigation issues, broken controls, console errors, and visual defects with evidence paths.

output_examples.input: Test a static marketing page for polish issues.
output_examples.output: A concise list of visible defects with annotated screenshots and no unnecessary repro videos.

best_practices: Use a staging or test environment when possible.
Provide a narrow scope for critical workflows and user roles.
Review captured evidence for sensitive data before sharing it.
anti_patterns: Do not run against systems you do not own or have permission to test.
Do not provide production credentials unless the evidence path is secured.
Do not ask for vague testing without a target URL or workflow scope.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a Markdown dogfood report with severity counts, issue details, screenshots, videos, and reproduction steps.

faq.question: Does it inspect application source code?
faq.answer: No. The skill tests the web app through the browser as a user would.

faq.question: Can it test authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can sign in with credentials you provide and ask for OTP codes when needed.

faq.question: Where are screenshots and videos stored?
faq.answer: They are stored in the selected output directory, usually under dogfood-output unless you choose another path.

faq.question: Is this a security testing skill?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on product QA, UX defects, console errors, and reproducible browser-level bugs.

faq.question: What should I check before sharing the report?
faq.answer: Review screenshots, videos, and auth-state files for secrets, personal data, and private customer information.
